quote: offers $X to put the family name on the School of Y — permanently ... The check clears immediately
why: cash += amount and name/donorSurname set on accept (data/eventData.ts:453-464); donor-named halls leave the offer pool (eventData.ts:262-266)

quote: $X in cash now, the school permanently renamed ... a 5-point dent ... that heals
why: apply adds the cash, dents 5 and renames (eventData.ts:453-464); donor text survives a lost dedication (systems/techtree/schools.ts:61-62); the dent drifts back at 5%/wk (systems/satisfaction/satisfactionSystem.ts:22)

quote: Nothing changes. The building keeps its name.
why: apply only logs (eventData.ts:475-477)

quote: they want the college to charter a Hellenic Council and permit Greek-letter organizations
why: offered once there are 2 clubs (eventData.ts:370,495); the count is read live (eventData.ts:497)

quote: Chapters begin forming from here on, each petitioning for recognition in the summer's Students beat
why: sets hellenicCouncilApproved (eventData.ts:507); chapter petitions go through the summer digest (data/studentLifeData.ts:986-991; systems/admissions/resolveAdmissions.ts:92)

quote: Chapters begin forming from here on
why: a chapter also needs 900 enrolled students per chapter (studentLifeData.ts:41,960-962,986-991); the council can come at 2 clubs (~440 students), so none may form for years

quote: A chapter is worth 2.5 points of social satisfaction against a club's fraction of that
why: 2.5 and 0.6 are raw points on the social attribute (studentLifeData.ts:59-60); past 20 raw points each is discounted (studentLifeData.ts:1166-1170), social clamps at 100 (satisfactionSystem.ts:195-199), and the headline gets ~24% of it (satisfactionSystem.ts:26-32)

quote: No fraternity or sorority will ever form at the college, and you will not be asked again. Clubs are unaffected.
why: only hellenicCouncilOffered is set (eventData.ts:519); eligible() needs !offered (495); canFormChapter needs approved (studentLifeData.ts:988); nothing else writes either flag

quote: N members, chartered in Year Y ... Counsel and a communications firm will see the chapter through for $X
why: amount = 1.8 weeks of opex fixed at fire time (eventData.ts:540); membership read live (eventData.ts:545)

quote: $X up front. X keeps its charter and everything it contributes; satisfaction takes a 3-point dent
why: cost = amount (eventData.ts:555); dent 3 (eventData.ts:557); the chapter is untouched

quote: No cash spent. X is dissolved permanently: N points of social satisfaction and $Y a week of cost go with it
why: for a housed chapter apply also takes its 40 beds out of capacity and tears down the house (eventData.ts:579-581); the describe (eventData.ts:568-574) lists satisfaction and cost only

quote: N points of social satisfaction ... go with it
why: raw figure (eventData.ts:570-572); the real loss comes after the student-life curve and the 100 cap and can be near zero (studentLifeData.ts:1166-1170; tabs/StudentLifeTab.tsx:89-95)

quote: The college's share of the build is $X
why: cost = 3.5 weeks of opex (eventData.ts:605,619)

quote: $X up front and $Y a week to run it, forever ... adds 40 beds ..., both effective immediately — the house itself is revealed in the build menu
why: housed set, upkeep += the same weekly figure, capacity += 40, a zero-cost house Buildable pushed as available (eventData.ts:620-648)

quote: a further 1.5 points of social satisfaction
why: raw figure, subject to the same curve and cap (studentLifeData.ts:61,1152-1170)

quote: a 2-point satisfaction dent ... will not ask again
why: housingAsked set (eventData.ts:662) and filtered out (eventData.ts:274-276); dent 2 (eventData.ts:663)

quote: has been on at you about T: it has been running without a R ... will not be on the open market for long
why: needs an AD and a vacant chair (eventData.ts:686); the coach is rolled at fire time and lost if declined (eventData.ts:695-709); "on at you" is a British idiom

quote: N takes the R's chair at quality Q — better than the market usually turns up
why: the rolled coach is seated (eventData.ts:734-735); best of 3 by potential (eventData.ts:698-702) against the market's journeyman floor (systems/athletics/athleticsSystem.ts:35-39)

quote: $S/yr thereafter
why: staff pay is charged x the athletics tier's upkeepMultiplier 0.75/1.0/1.4 (studentLifeData.ts:284-288,1124-1131) and rises with tenure (athleticsSystem.ts:44-49)

quote: The chair stays empty ... which costs the team quality for as long as it takes
why: an empty chair scores COACH_VACANCY_QUALITY in coaching quality (studentLifeData.ts:638-642)

quote: self-report and take the season's ban, or ... fight it — $X in lawyers, and no promise
why: needs an AD and a flagship program (eventData.ts:756); amount = 2 weeks of opex (eventData.ts:766)

quote: barred from the postseason through Year Y; a 3-point dent
why: sets postseasonBanThroughYear by the same rule (eventData.ts:778-781); banned teams sit out (systems/athletics/playoffs.ts:93)

quote: Half the time ... no ban follows; the other half ... two seasons with a 5-point dent
why: random() < 0.5 (eventData.ts:792); ban through year+1 (eventData.ts:795); dent 5 (eventData.ts:797)

quote: offered the head job at a bigger program ... A retention package of $X would keep them
why: head coaches at quality 75+ with 2+ years (eventData.ts:333-345); package = 60% of salary (eventData.ts:820)

quote: $X now, and C stays with T
why: cost charged by the reducer, apply logs (eventData.ts:828-831); the same coach can be asked about again after the 156-week repeat cooldown (eventData.ts:183)

quote: C leaves ... the market will list somebody for it next week
why: headCoach cleared (eventData.ts:840); the weekly market lists a journeyman for every uncovered open chair (athleticsSystem.ts:35-39; studentLifeData.ts:584-592)

quote: R has passed C in this year's table ... either would cost $X
why: fired once per passing rival above prestige 100 (systems/events/eventSystem.ts:164-181); both paid choices cost amount (eventData.ts:896,911); "table" is British usage

quote: $X up front, and $S/yr thereafter
why: S is the base salary; payroll pays S x marketRateMultiplier (systems/finance/financeSystem.ts:235-237), 2.5x-4x at the prestige over 100 this event needs (data/facultyData.ts:619-625; eventSystem.ts:166); every other appointment shows the paid rate (tabs/FacultyTab.tsx:186; systems/faculty/appointments.ts:19); the log repeats the base (eventData.ts:902)

quote: Endow the chair / "an endowed chair in F"
why: nothing is endowed: the up-front sum is spent and the salary is ordinary payroll (eventData.ts:896-902)

quote: $X committed; $2.2X into the endowment ... feeds the financial-resources input to prestige
why: endowment += round(2.2 x amount) (eventData.ts:913-914); endowment is a weighted prestige input (systems/prestige/prestigeSystem.ts:68,406)

quote: Nothing is spent. The college answers on the field, or does not.
why: apply only logs (eventData.ts:923)

quote: wants varsity status: real recruiting, a paid coach, and a conference schedule
why: no recruiting lever exists (the pot's funding band stands in, studentLifeData.ts:648-658) and there are no conferences, only a national 8-team bracket (playoffs.ts:7-17)

quote: $X up front for a program budget (prompt: "Establishing the program costs $X")
why: apply also sets a permanent weekly program upkeep of 0.003 weeks of opex (eventData.ts:387,977), charged every week even while awaiting the venue (studentLifeData.ts:1121-1131); neither text mentions a running cost

quote: a 2-point satisfaction dent ... will petition again in 3 years
why: varsityLastAskedYear set (eventData.ts:996); eligible again after 3 years (studentLifeData.ts:888-892)

quote: counts toward curriculum breadth — the largest input ... weighted there above its course count, though still inside that input's cap
why: breadth weight 50 is the largest term (prestigeSystem.ts:52); professional prestigeWeight 1.4-2.0 against 1.0, inside GRADUATE_PROGRAM_SHARE (prestigeSystem.ts:80-94; data/techData.ts:477,497,513)

quote: A research degree counts toward curriculum breadth AND toward the college's research standing
why: doctoral programs add DOCTORATE_PRESTIGE_CREDIT to research credits (prestigeSystem.ts:186-205); the MFA is typed doctoral, so it too is called "a research degree" (techData.ts:601)

quote: the hall they share is S Hall. The name is permanent
why: the school's founding is never revoked (schools.ts:46-54), but the "S Hall" label is live and reverts to the seeded name if a program moves out (schools.ts:56-65)

quote: the heaviest single contribution curriculum breadth can make ... graduate programs open in the capital project built to house them
why: one school = 0.25/7 of breadth against at most 0.15 x 2/12 for one graduate program (prestigeSystem.ts:77-94); the graduate gate needs the host standing (techData.ts:649-655)

quote: Every tier-2 course ... finished ... counts toward curriculum breadth from now on ... its tier-3 catalog is open
why: awarded when every tier-2 id is done (systems/techtree/techSystem.ts:589-596); PROGRAM_ESTABLISHED_SHARE (prestigeSystem.ts:77)

quote: All nine courses ... are done ... a further, separate share of curriculum breadth
why: awarded when tier 3 is done (techSystem.ts:599-606); PROGRAM_DISTINGUISHED_SHARE (prestigeSystem.ts:78)

quote: Founders Hall is where every program begins, and most will not stay
why: canFoundProgram accepts any academic hall with a free slot (techSystem.ts:399-405), and letter a-school-grows tells the player to found programs straight into the school's hall (eventData.ts:1229); the counts are right (data/foundingData.ts:34,46-47)

quote: six rooms, three quarters of a million, sixteen weeks to build
why: Elm Hall costs $2,500,000 and takes 26 weeks (techData.ts:77-79,809-816); stale since the Plan 71 retune (commit a80c989 changed 750_000/16 to 2_500_000/26)

quote: Housing is not a cap on how many we admit ... next summer's applicants hear it
why: enrollment is not bed-gated; beds scale the pool from a 0.35 floor and feed satisfaction, which word of mouth reads (systems/admissions/admissionsSystem.ts:75-82,111-116)

quote: it is set blind, it locks, and the class that pays it pays it for four years
why: three beats (state/types.ts:490); price set blind and locked before the reveal (components/InterruptModal.tsx:219-223,254-270); each class keeps its price (financeSystem.ts:241-249)

quote: out of Founders Hall a move is four weeks dark, not the twelve ... more than any other school, so S moves first
why: FOUNDERS_MOVE_WEEKS 4, RELOCATION_WEEKS 12 (techSystem.ts:448-457); nextSchoolToMove (schools.ts:154-163)

quote: E is S's from then on
why: a claim is a live reading: another school's program founded into the hall, or the hall emptied, ends it (schools.ts:87-103)

quote: found every new S program straight into H ... Six S programs in H found the School of S, and the hall takes its name
why: founding into any academic hall (techSystem.ts:399-405); dedication founds the school and relabels the hall (techSystem.ts:575-582; schools.ts:61-65)

quote: there are six halls for seven schools, and the last school sorted keeps Founders Hall as its own
why: six hall names (techData.ts:85-88), seven schools (techData.ts:118-200); foundersIsHome (schools.ts:105-112)

quote: When each has finished one, the Research Park opens
why: the park also waits for Year 12 (data/projectData.ts:60; systems/estate/projects.ts:30,35), and a school's labs can all finish years earlier

quote: the Graduate College opens once any school teaches every one of its courses
why: it also waits for Year 15 (projectData.ts:68; projects.ts:30)

quote: laboratories for rent to companies who want to be near the faculty
why: the park earns no rent: $45,000/wk upkeep and a research lift only (projectData.ts:57-61)

quote: It is where Landmark research is commissioned
why: the park only unlocks the tier; a Landmark Program still runs in a lab (data/researchData.ts:268-276; systems/research/startInitiative.ts:16,25)

quote: Three hundred and fifty students ..., five professors ... the clock will not run until you have
why: FOUNDING_BODY 350 (foundingData.ts:34); five founding faculty (state/actions.ts:372-400); openingHoldsClock (state/opening.ts:31-33)

quote: the ground is yours, so this one costs nothing
why: siting the already-built Founders Hall charges nothing (state/placeBuildable.ts:28-32)

quote: three programs, two courses each, and a professor on every one ... A program is a row of nine courses
why: FOUNDING_COURSES_PER_PROGRAM 2 (foundingData.ts:47); nine courses per major (techData.ts:102-106)

quote: each is developed — paid for once
why: development is paid once, but every course then costs weekly upkeep and instruction sections (financeSystem.ts:100-121,177-181)

quote: N programs are on offer, and founding one starts its first course with the professor you pick
why: PROGRAM_OFFER_COUNT 3 (systems/techtree/programOffers.ts:29); foundProgram starts the entry course with the chosen teacher (techSystem.ts:383-387)

quote: the first program the college has chosen ... which the Dean regards as a healthy sign
why: flavor only (data/foundingNotes.ts:1-5; components/FoundingNotes.tsx:26-32); no Dean seat exists before a school is founded (data/seatData.ts:154-162); "common room" is British

quote: Until this week the college emptied at five o'clock; now there is ... a rota for the kitchen
why: flavor; every founding student commutes (foundingData.ts:28-31); "rota" is British

quote: spent more than it took in for two terms running
why: Deficit = two or more deficit terms in a row (systems/finance/distress.ts:108,139-140)

quote: The board would like to see a surplus before it sees another building
why: nothing blocks or scores building at Deficit: only Freeze and Austerity stop construction (distress.ts:73-76), and confidence reads only the term result (distress.ts:181-189)

quote: Until it has run two surplus terms with money in the bank, ... no new construction and no borrowing
why: constructionFrozen/borrowingAllowed (distress.ts:73-80); recovered() (distress.ts:113-115); courses exempt (techSystem.ts:256)

quote: cutting maintenance to nothing, and will not let the listed tuition fall
why: maintenance 0 at Austerity (distress.ts:154); tuitionFloor (distress.ts:84-86; resolveAdmissions.ts:90); after three frozen terms (distress.ts:127)

quote: until the books are in surplus again
why: exit needs two surplus terms in a row and cash above zero (distress.ts:113-115,123); one surplus term does not lift it

quote: an interim chief financial officer for three years, who will set the endowment draw and the maintenance budget ... The college will remember this
why: 9 terms (distress.ts:37); draw 5%, maintenance 50% (distress.ts:155-158); the scar is recorded (distress.ts:193) and read by the report and alumni memory (state/finalReport.ts:133; data/alumniData.ts:32)

quote: maintenance goes back to what the administration had set, and the tuition is the administration's again
why: exit via recovered() (distress.ts:123,142); own settings restored (distress.ts:159-166)

quote: The interim CFO's three years are up. The draw and the maintenance budget are the administration's again
why: fixed sentence (distress.ts:119-121,141)

quote: set where they were before the appointment
why: restores the settings saved when austerity began, before the board's cuts, not those in force at the appointment (distress.ts:150-153,159-166)

quote: more than a year of its expenses in cash for a year ... keep half a year ... each quarter, until the endowment is as strong as the guidebooks measure
why: 52 weeks over 52 weeks; sweep keeps 26 weeks, runs every 13, capped at the full mark (systems/finance/sweep.ts:25-33,54-59,68-90)

quote: will not raise it again for a decade
why: IDLE_REMINDER_YEARS 10 (sweep.ts:33,86-87)

quote: paying its way again, with reserves to cover a term ... with its confidence
why: sent on reaching Sound from Deficit or worse (distress.ts:143); Sound needs a term's expenses in cash (distress.ts:109-110); +2 confidence (distress.ts:184)

quote: The queue at the dining halls runs out of the door and round the building ... They want X open, and they want a date
why: the ask is the next available basic-needs building (systems/demands/demandSystem.ts:118-123); 78-week deadline (demandSystem.ts:322-333); "queue" and "round" are British

quote: a sit-in in the reading room has produced a single written demand: X
why: flavor; the ask is the next academic-need building (demandSystem.ts:118-123); "corridors" leans British

quote: The student body has asked, formally, for X
why: same derivation (demandSystem.ts:134-158)

quote: The wait for an appointment at the health service is measured in weeks
why: health is asked for only above the health gate (demandSystem.ts:137)

quote: Every bed on campus is spoken for and the waiting list is longer than the incoming class
why: raised only when bed coverage is short (demandSystem.ts:162-180); the waiting list is flavor

quote: open X, and stop admitting people there is no seat for
why: met at one more course's worth of seats (demandSystem.ts:184-205); admissions already clip the class to the seats left (systems/techtree/instructionCapacity.ts:53-67)

quote: students served by dining / "beds of campus housing" / "seats across the catalog"
why: each matches the reading demandProgress compares (demandSystem.ts:61-74)

quote: raised a formal demand: ..., within 78 weeks
why: DEMAND_DEADLINE_WEEKS (data/demandData.ts:30; demandSystem.ts:325,332)

quote: X is open, and the campus knows who asked for it
why: met on any rise in the served figure (another building of that need, a chapter house's 40 beds, a dorm's added floors), so X may not be open (demandSystem.ts:61-74,271-275; eventData.ts:630)

quote: Word of it will follow the college into next year's admissions
why: -8 to the stock, which the trailing-year average read by word of mouth captures (demandSystem.ts:278-282; satisfactionSystem.ts:384-385; admissionsSystem.ts:11-15)

quote: has passed with nothing built
why: also logged when something was built but fell short of the target (demandSystem.ts:278-281)

why: goal schoolsOver 4, read at the due summer (data/promiseData.ts:41; systems/events/catalogue.ts:101; systems/promises/promises.ts:72)

quote: A thousand students on the lawn
why: enrolledOver 1000, not scaled (promiseData.ts:54; catalogue.ts:88)

quote: A hundred million in the fund / kept "A hundred million"
why: endowmentOver is multiplied by priceScale (0.2-12, annual opex / $15M) when judged (catalogue.ts:43-46,147,156-159): the real bar runs from $20M to $1.2B; the panel shows only the title (tabs/PromisesPanel.tsx:57,108-111)

quote: The best teaching in the state
why: no college is compared: the goal is a campus average course score of 44, a C (promiseData.ts:80; catalogue.ts:119; data/courseQuality.ts:20)

quote: kept "The teaching is what the college is known for"
why: known for is the identity-tag mechanic (tabs/IdentityPanel.tsx:18); keeping the promise grants no Teaching College tag (promises.ts:72-75)

quote: Not one building on the register
why: backlogUnder 1 (x scale, a few dollars) over standing buildings (promiseData.ts:93; catalogue.ts:111)

quote: Owing nothing to anybody
why: debtUnder 1 (x scale) (promiseData.ts:106; catalogue.ts:107); "refinanced twice" is backstory

quote: eleven programs, each taught properly / kept "every one of them is taught"
why: the goal counts housed programs only; staffing and teaching quality are not read (promiseData.ts:119; catalogue.ts:65-67,99)

quote: kept "The campus is what the architect said it could be, fifteen years on"
why: the promise falls due 12 years after it is made (promiseData.ts:133; promises.ts:128); planting is a real lever (engine/reducer.ts:279-291; systems/estate/beauty.ts:57-58)

quote: a decade of doing the unglamorous thing
why: the term is 12 years (promiseData.ts:146); reunions are the real lever (systems/alumni/giving.ts:142-158)

quote: {college} admits most of those who apply
why: offered at an admit rate as low as 45% (selectivityUnder 0.55: promiseData.ts:157; catalogue.ts:121-122)

quote: Out of the hole by the decade's end
why: due 8 years after acceptance, whatever the decade (promiseData.ts:172; promises.ts:128)

quote: missed "The date came. The college was still in the hole."
why: the goal also needs board confidence 70+ (promiseData.ts:171): a college back at Sound with confidence 69 is told it is still in the hole; that condition is shown nowhere (PromisesPanel.tsx:108-111)

quote: thirty of them, properly paid, in a decade
why: the term is 12 years (promiseData.ts:185)

quote: Thirty scholars worth the name / "properly paid"
why: the goal is a headcount of 30; pay and quality are not read (catalogue.ts:91)

quote: Two thousand graduates on the rolls
why: alumniOver 2000 (promiseData.ts:197; catalogue.ts:68,90)

quote: publishing the figure every year until it is one the college would print
why: flavor; the goal is satisfaction 64+ at the due summer (promiseData.ts:210; catalogue.ts:115)

quote: Ten million in reserve / kept "Ten million in the reserve"
why: cashOver is multiplied by priceScale when judged (catalogue.ts:147,156-159): $10M x scale, from $2M to $120M

quote: A hundred and twenty-five million in the fund
why: endowmentOver is multiplied by priceScale when judged (catalogue.ts:147,156-159): $125M x scale, from $25M to $1.5B

quote: would like the campaign to be judged by it
why: no campaign is tied to the promise and none is read when it is judged (promises.ts:72; systems/alumni/campaigns.ts)

quote: Twelve buildings
why: buildingsOver counts every standing building, dorm or facility, including statues, fountains, gardens, quads and courts (catalogue.ts:64,94; state/types.ts:386)

quote: Two thousand students
why: enrolledOver 2000 (promiseData.ts:262)

quote: a decade of the slow work
why: the term is 12 years (promiseData.ts:276)

quote: those eight hundred as content as the few hundred are now
why: the goal is a fixed satisfaction of 50+, not the level at the time the promise is made (promiseData.ts:288)

quote: Borrowing under eight million / kept "below eight million"
why: debtUnder is multiplied by priceScale when judged (catalogue.ts:147,156-159): $8M x scale, from $1.6M to $96M

quote: Twenty programs would make {college} the college a school-leaver can choose
why: programsOver 20 (promiseData.ts:314); "school-leaver" and "prospectus" are British

quote: Teaching worth the fee
why: goal campus average 30+, a D (promiseData.ts:327; courseQuality.ts:21); "the fee" is British for tuition

quote: kept "The fee is still high"
why: tuition is not read when the promise is judged; a college that cut its price still hears it (promises.ts:72)

quote: Five hundred students
why: enrolledOver 500 (promiseData.ts:340)

quote: A college people recommend
why: reads as word of mouth (satisfaction), but the goal is prestige 87+ (reputationOver 58 x 1.5: promiseData.ts:353; catalogue.ts:81,124)

quote: raise one great building, the kind a campus is photographed by
why: only capital projects count (projectsOver: catalogue.ts:112); the grand landmarks, "the college on every postcard", carry no project and do not keep it (data/facilitiesData.ts:457-474,911-926)

quote: The board has put something on the record: {title}.
why: it is only an offer until taken; leaving the beat declines it at no cost (promises.ts:118-134)

quote: Accepted, publicly: {title}. {years} years.
why: promises.ts:128-129

quote: Declined: {title}.
why: added to the declined list, rested 4 years (promises.ts:131; promiseData.ts:33)

quote: {line}
why: the log carries the promise's own kept/missed line (promises.ts:75)

quote: {years} years left / "Due next year" / "Due this summer"
why: tabs/PromisesPanel.tsx:10-15

why: decade list at Years 10-40, picks = room left (promises.ts:37-39,84-93,111-115; PromisesPanel.tsx:96)

quote: Aim for this / "Chosen"
why: labels (PromisesPanel.tsx:109); decadeTake is never rendered

quote: Nothing promised, and nothing owed.
why: PromisesPanel.tsx:19

why: PROMISE_CAP 3 (promiseData.ts:25); never shown, since no offer is made without room (promises.ts:78-81; PromisesPanel.tsx:116)

quote: Declining costs nothing; keeping it is worth more than that.
why: a decline applies no effect; rewards are positive (promises.ts:72-75,131)

quote: Everyone being asked lived three to a room

quote: A campaign for endowed chairs: money that pays a salary forever / missed "short of the chairs it was named for"
why: the money goes into the general endowment; no chair or salary is endowed (campaigns.ts:75)

quote: no building, no plaque, nothing to photograph
why: endowment campaign (campaignData.ts:71; campaigns.ts:75); "four bad years" matches its resonance list (campaignData.ts:74)

quote: three hundred alumni, and housing under 70 etc.
why: each matches its when() (campaignData.ts:45-81); the field is never rendered

quote: Takes the choice that spends least.

quote: Takes the choice that spends most, which is usually the one that fixes it.
why: seats.ts:167-168; catalogueEngine.ts:72

quote: The first seat a college fills
why: no order is enforced; any seat can be filled first (seats.ts:59-63)

quote: Keep the faculty with you
why: the popular rule reads student satisfaction; there is no faculty sentiment (seats.ts:169)

quote: One for each school ... Takes the academic routine when there is no Provost; with a Provost, three of them let the year run at eight times
why: one slot per founded school (seats.ts:31-38); handlerFor (seats.ts:150-154); fastestAllowed (seats.ts:130-132)

quote: Keep the department happy
why: student satisfaction only (seats.ts:169)

quote: Roofs, boilers, kitchens and storms: ... answered before they reach the President's desk
